newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias up 14.29 pct on lingering takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: Victorias up 14.29 pct on lingering takeover talk.

text.p: Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Co hit an intra-day high of 4.80 pesos on Thursday amid persistent talk the company may receive a takeover or stake purchase offer, brokers said.
Shares of the sugar miller gained 60 centavos, or 14.29 percent in late trade on Thursday.

"Victorias has said it is looking for a strategic partner and talks about San Miguel and Lucio Tan being interested added fuel to the fire," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
"Since yesterday, there were reports that Lucio Tan and San Miguel were eyeing Victorias," Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc said.

In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange on Thursday, Victorias said that it has no knowledge of reports that food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp and Filipino-Chinese tycoon Lucio Tan were interested in the company, said a broker who said he received a copy of Victorias' statement.
Victorias officials could not immediately be reached for comment. Names of a number of potential suitors and possible equity buyers for Victorias have cropped up this week.
The sugar miller last week disclosed debt problems, and has obtained a 90-day moratarium from its creditors on principal repayments covering $168 million in loans.
